title: PeAD: Psychotherapy in early AD – A randomized controlled pilot study
summary: In this study, we are investigating the feasibility and acceptance of a 10-session psychotherapeutic intervention program for people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and their care partners. The goal of the intervention is to improve disease acceptance. Techniques from cognitive behavioral therapy and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) are used. The two sessions for family members focus on stress management, planning for the future, and self-care. The control intervention consists of psychoeducational sessions on aging and dementia. Through focus group interviews, we collect detailed feedback to tailor the program to the participants’ needs. In addition, we conduct surveys using questionnaires to measure the effects on the secondary endpoints mentioned above.

interventions.name: Intervention group: group-psychotherapy with 10 sessions each lasting 90 minutes, in addition 2 sessions lasting 90 min. are for care partners only
Control group: group-psychotherapy with 10 sessions each lasting 90 minutes, in addition 2 sessions lasting 90 min. are for care partners only

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria MCI patients:
• Clinical diagnosis of MCI according to the NIA-AA criteria (Albert et al., 2011) ≥3 months and ≤24 months prior to randomization
• Memory performance: ≤1.5 standard deviations below the age-, sex-, and education-adjusted norm group in ≥1 cognitive domain
• Cerebrospinal fluid evidence of Alzheimer’s disease (abnormal pTau and pTau181/Aβ42 or Aβ42/Aβ40 levels)
• Activities of daily living (ADLs) preserved
• Written informed consent from the patient
• Accompaniment by a primary care partner who is also willing to participate in the study
• Age ≥ 60 years

Inclusion criteria Care Partners:
- Written declaration of consent
- Regular contact with the patient
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria MCI patients:
• Insufficient knowledge of the German language
• Illiteracy
• Dementia (MMST < 22 points)
• Severe depression (GDS ≥ 8 points)
• Severe anxiety symptoms (GAI ≥ 11 points)
• Acute suicidal ideation
• Evidence of a non-Alzheimer’s disease (non-AD) neurodegenerative disorder, such as: Parkinson’s disease, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal lobar degeneration, or very rapid cognitive decline within a few weeks or months (classically suggestive of a prion disease, neoplasm, or metabolic disorder)
• Brain tumor
• Evidence of cerebrovascular disease on structural imaging, suggesting a vascular cause of the cognitive impairments

Exclusion criteria Care Partners:
- Illiteracy
